findings.note: The H2 asks 'What can delay or block the sale?' but the opening paragraph spends four sentences on framing ('The real question is whether the house or the paperwork is the bigger risk to the sale. Some of it comes from the house. A lot of it comes from the paperwork and the people. Sort those apart early...') and only says 'Three things can stall the sale of a packed house' as its last sentence, without naming them. Change the opening so the first sentence answers directly, for example by naming the three causes (a local health or fire official's attention, a disclosure misstep, and authority, heir or lien problems that surface late), then keep the house-versus-paperwork framing after it. Add no new facts.
'not you and not me' uses a first-person 'me' that is not otherwise established in the section; consider 'not you and not the writer of this guide' or simply 'not you'.
'near Oakland' is supported only by the link plan anchor; fine as is, but the sentence gives no claim that Oakland rules apply to the reader's property. Keep it framed as background.

required_actions: Rewrite the first sentence(s) of the opening paragraph so the answer (the three things that can delay or block the sale) comes first, before the house-versus-paperwork framing.
